chunks: And it is narrated from Rawḥ ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Exalted:
"Men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah."

He عليه السلام said: "They were people of trade, but when the salat (prayer) became due, they left the trade and went to the salat (prayer), and they are greater in reward than one who did not engage in trade."

key_terms.أَصْحَابَ تِجَارَةٍ: people engaged in business and livelihood
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the salat (prayer) that becomes due at its appointed time
key_terms.ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ: the remembrance of Allah, including conscious devotion and worship

ai.seo_question: Who are the men described in the Qur'an as not being distracted by trade or sale from the remembrance of Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the verse praises believers who participate in trade yet do not let worldly business distract them from the remembrance of Allah and the performance of salat (prayer). Their merit is especially great because they leave profitable activity when prayer time arrives, showing obedience and priority for worship over livelihood.
